summary: A skier and a snowboarder, with their dog, triggered an avalanche on the northeast face of Mount Peck south of Monarch Crest around 4 p.m.; the skier deployed an airbag pack and was partially buried, the snowboarder was nearly fully buried but kept a hand above the snowpack and the skier dug her out. Both refused medical care and hiked out on their own; the dog was not recovered that day but was found alive near the top of Monarch Pass two days later and reunited with its owners.
location: northeast face of Mount Peck, south of Monarch Crest
notes: Heart of the Rockies Radio (opened run 601): CCSAR-South paged out ~5:20 Thursday evening via a friend's text from the subjects. Date pinned 2022-03-10 (verified Thursday): SnowBrains/AAC 'Mid-Tour Change of Plans' accounts date the slide 'March 10th'/'March 10, 2022' (CAIC-credited; hard slab, 40-degree north-facing slope, broke 3-5 ft deep on facets buried by the Feb 21 storm). Humans uninjured.
